formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature, the owner's LINK allowance for the spender is set to exactly `value`. This replaces the old allowance (ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit -> _approve(owner, spender, value)).
The owner's permit nonce goes up by one, which voids any other signed permit that uses the same nonce.
The signature is accepted only until `deadline` (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)). The allowance it sets does not expire.
No tokens move at signing. The spender can later pull up to `value` LINK from the owner with transferFrom.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender as a hex address, the max amount in LINK (resolved from the verifying contract, 'Unlimited' at 2^255 or above), the deadline as a date, and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line names no amount, token or spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json format Permit: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens" and no interpolatedIntent. Case 0 screen intent is just 'Authorize spending of tokens'. The 25 LINK and spender 0x1111…0582 appear only in the fields.
